how_to_use: Every row is a proposal, not an implemented change except where status says IMPLEMENTED. Impact, effort and risk are this session's judgement and are labelled as judgement. Prerequisites name the questions (Q-ids in the decision register) that must be answered first. Choose a path, then set its status to accepted/maybe/rejected in this file; the page re-renders from this JSON and nothing else.

verdict_key.IMPLEMENTED: already built in nfl-edge/ and visible on this site
verdict_key.NEEDS DECISION: cannot proceed without an owner answer

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the negative result first and loudly: the front page states that 0 of 4 strategies qualify and shows the closing-line MAE gap in one line.
suggestions.why: The single most useful decision input is 'this does not work yet'. Hiding it wastes the next three months of effort on a dead end and is how betting projects normally fail.

suggestions.suggestion: Change the target from 'beat the spread' to 'beat the total, narrowly, and only in high-variance spots' - our total model is 0.36 points behind the closing line versus 0.63 for the spread, and its holdout ROI (-5.3%) is less bad than the moneyline (-8.5%).
suggestions.why: Pick the fight where the gap is smallest. The totals market has fewer public-data participants than sides.
suggestions.note: Must be pre-registered as a new gate version before it is run, otherwise it is a post-hoc search.

suggestions.suggestion: Decide what the project is for: (a) a rigorous 'no-edge' research lab, (b) a data-coverage and decision-support product, or (c) a hunt for proprietary signal that requires licensed data. The measured evidence supports (a) or (b) today, not (c) without budget.
suggestions.why: Every other priority depends on this answer (Q22).

suggestions.suggestion: Freeze ten pre-registered gates in a versioned JSON file and evaluate them unchanged, with a placebo/permutation test and season-stability requirement as the anti-luck core.
suggestions.why: Gates are the only thing separating a leaderboard from a highlight reel. Versioning stops 'move the goalposts until it passes'.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a formal multiple-testing correction across the whole strategy family (Benjamini-Hochberg) and report q-values next to each placebo p-value.
suggestions.why: Four strategies were tested here; if the catalogue grows to twenty, a p<0.05 will appear by chance. The NBA workspace already does BH-FDR, so the method is available in-repo.
suggestions.note: Not implemented here because the placebo p-values are all far from significance (0.37-0.63); a correction would change no conclusion, so it was left as a proposal rather than claimed as done.

suggestions.suggestion: Reconcile every game archive against the official standings before using it, and refuse to publish if the aggregate check fails.
suggestions.why: It caught a real 16-game hole in the peer archive (weeks 8-9) that would have skewed every rate statistic.

suggestions.suggestion: Publish the official Week 10 injury report per club, with practice and game status, and explicitly state that no starter/backup label exists in that source.
suggestions.why: The honest version of the injury requirement: it shows what the league actually discloses so the gap is visible rather than papered over.

suggestions.suggestion: Obtain a licensed depth chart + snap counts and build a 'starter-out weight' per club: expected minutes lost by position, then regress margin on it.
suggestions.why: This is the only way to answer the backup-deficiency question with numbers instead of adjectives.
suggestions.note: Requires budget or a licence; cannot be done from nfl.com alone.

suggestions.suggestion: Capture a point-in-time snapshot of the official injury report daily (Wed/Thu/Fri) instead of once, because availability news moves the line and a single crawl cannot show the move.
suggestions.why: Without the timestamp sequence you cannot test the only form of injury edge that plausibly exists: being faster than the price.
suggestions.note: Needs a scheduled job and a price source to compare against.

suggestions.suggestion: One dashboard with category subpages, every table row carrying a source link, and a build script that fails if a row has no source or a link is broken.
suggestions.why: A reader can audit any number in two clicks; a broken link or unsourced row cannot reach the live site.

suggestions.suggestion: Consolidate the repository. Twenty parallel workspaces with duplicated dashboards (and three competing SF rental sites) make it impossible for a reader to know which number is current.
suggestions.why: Duplication is now a correctness risk, not just clutter: two dashboards can disagree and both claim 'verified'.

suggestions.suggestion: Keep a decision register that separates ANSWERED from OPEN, and block each major decision on named questions (D1-D7).
suggestions.why: It converts 'we should think about it' into a checklist with a stopping condition.

suggestions.suggestion: Publish a one-page methodology PDF for each released model version: inputs, freeze date, gate results, and the exact commit hash.
suggestions.why: Makes the leaderboard reproducible by a third party, which is the only substitute for trust.

suggestions.suggestion: Test the one signal we can measure cheaply and that the market may under-price: rest/short-week asymmetry (Thursday games, off a Monday game).
suggestions.why: It needs only the schedule we already have plus results; it is a genuinely different information set from 'team strength', which the market already nails.
suggestions.note: Not implemented this session: the schedule-to-rest join must be built from official week pages and pre-registered before any result is shown.

suggestions.suggestion: Keep reward points non-monetary with zero cash value, and carry the NCPG helpline on every page.
suggestions.why: A monetary leaderboard on an unvalidated model is an advertisement for losing money.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a second, independent official check per data point where one exists: e.g. cross-check each game score against the club page and the league scoreboard on the same date.
suggestions.why: A transcription error in a single source is invisible to every internal consistency test we run. Two independent official renderings would catch it.
